slides: Welcome back, and now a new topic, motion.

slides.say: Motion questions come up in almost every exam. Cars, trains, runners and boats all cover some distance in some time.

slides: And the good news is that you already know the idea, from work and rate.

slides.say: Remember the work formula? Rate times time is equal to work.
at: Rate times time is equal to work

slides.say: In motion, the work is the distance we cover. And the rate is our speed.
In work, a machine packs twenty-five boxes an hour.
In motion, a car covers twenty-five kilometers an hour. It's the same idea, with new names.
at: a car covers twenty-five kilometers an hour

slides.say: So the motion formula is this. Distance is equal to speed times time.
at: Distance is equal to speed times time

slides.say: The speed is the distance we cover in one unit of time. Kilometers per hour means how many kilometers we cover in one hour.
Let's see it in numbers. A cyclist rides at fifteen kilometers per hour, for three hours. How far does she ride?
at: A cyclist rides at fifteen kilometers per hour

slides: Fifteen kilometers per hour means fifteen kilometers in each hour. So every hour adds fifteen more kilometers.

slides.say: Three hours is fifteen times three, forty-five. So she rides forty-five kilometers.

slides: So to find the distance, we multiply the speed by the time.

slides.say: If you're not sure when to multiply and when to divide, use the motion triangle.
The distance goes on top. The speed and the time go at the bottom, side by side.

slides: Now we cover the one we want. What's left tells us what to do.

slides.say: Cover the distance. The speed and the time are left, side by side. So the distance is the speed times the time.
at: So the distance is the speed times

slides.say: Cover the time. The distance is left, over the speed. So the time is the distance divided by the speed.
at: So the time is the distance divided

slides.say: And cover the speed. The distance is left, over the time. So the speed is the distance divided by the time.
at: So the speed is the distance divided

slides.say: If you know the formula by heart, that's enough. If you need the triangle, here it is.
Now a new example. A train travels a hundred twenty kilometers at forty kilometers per hour. How long does the trip take?
at: A train travels a hundred twenty kilometers

slides.say: They ask for the time. So we cover the time, and the time is the distance divided by the speed.
at: the time is the distance divided by the speed

slides.say: A hundred twenty divided by forty is three, because forty times three is a hundred twenty. So the trip takes three hours.
at: A hundred twenty divided by forty

slides.say: Now the other way. A bus travels a hundred fifty kilometers in two hours. What is its speed?
at: A bus travels a hundred fifty kilometers

slides.say: We cover the speed. The speed is the distance divided by the time.
at: The speed is the distance divided

slides.say: A hundred fifty divided by two is seventy-five. So the bus travels at seventy-five kilometers per hour.
at: A hundred fifty divided by two

slides.say: Let's check it. Seventy-five kilometers in each hour, for two hours, is a hundred fifty. That's the distance they gave us. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next part.
at: for two hours, is a hundred fifty
